title: The moon's low density, old material and rare metals don't fit an impact origin

tellings.quote: What's up with the moon? It is way less dense than the Earth. The material predates the Earth and yet it's supposed to have come from the Earth itself from some sort of asteroid impact.
And it's extremely challenging to get from a ring of debris around the Earth to the moon that we see today.
tellings.difference: Argues that it is mathematically hard to form the Moon from a debris ring, and also doubts the capture theory, rather than pointing to density, the age of the material and rare metals.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell the theory that the standard origin of the Moon, an Earth impact producing a debris ring, does not work. This telling answers the host's question about the Moon's origin.

as_told.title: Mathematical problems with the Moon's capture and impact origin theories

plain: This is the idea that the Moon does not fit the usual explanation, which is that it formed from material knocked off the Earth by a huge impact. Michels raises it himself, without naming a source: the Moon is much less dense than the Earth, and its material is older than the Earth, even though it supposedly came from the Earth. The researcher Randall Carlson argues it on different grounds in the same episode. He says it is very hard, mathematically, to get from a ring of debris around the Earth to the Moon we see today, and he doubts the other theory too, that the Earth captured the Moon. The questions are raised in an episode that asks whether the Moon could be an alien craft.
